newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: INTERVIEW-C&P sees huge mid-income housing demand.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW-C&P sees huge mid-income housing demand.

text.p: Philippine developer C&P Homes Inc aims to increase its market share in middle-income housing in view of the strong current demand, chief financial officer John Huang told Reuters on Friday.
Middle-income housing comprised 18 to 20 percent of C&P sales in 1995 and 4.0 percent in 1994. "This year, it will probably account for 30 percent," he said.

C&P, which normally specialises in low-cost housing, defines middle-income properties as those that cost about 1.0 million pesos. Philippine real estate giant Ayala Land defines mid-income houses as those in the 1.5 to 5.0 million peso range.

"The market has interpreted this as a massive shift in strategy. (But) we're still predominantly a low-cost housing developer. This segment of middle-income housing is a natural extension of our low-cost focus," he said.
He said demand for middle-range housing in the Philippines had risen due to improving incomes and an increased willingness by banks to provide financing.
Due to the higher proportion of middle-income housing, he said the company had revised its unit sales forecast this year to 25,000 from 27,000.
"The sales mix has improved," he said, adding that this did not mean a change in earnings targets for 1996.
"We think we will earn 2.7 billion pesos on revenues of 9.0 billion pesos. We're on track to meeting these targets," he said. In 1995, the company made a net income of 2.011 billion pesos.
For the first nine months of this year, "we expect it (net profit) close to 2.0 billion pesos. The topline will be about close to 7.0 billion pesos," he said.
Unit sales are expected to have reached 17,000 from January to September.
C&P posted a net income of 1.421 billion pesos from revenues of 4.968 billion pesos in the nine-month period last year.
The company aims to sell 30,000 housing units next year.
Net income could rise by 15 percent to 3.1 billion pesos next year, while revenues could increase by 22 percent to 11 billion pesos, he said.
C&P Homes has one of the largest land banks among Philippine housing developers, totalling about 3,100 hectares.
"We have enough land for the next five to eight years," Huang said.
